title: Willie Bryant's Southern tour: no food in Paintsville
summary: The band lived at the Savoy and Apollo, then toured the South; denied food, Ramirez bought groceries in Kentucky and the whole bus emptied.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: And how long did you stay with Willie Bryant?

Well, let me see. We lived in the Savoy and we lived in the Apollo! -- because Willie was popular there. Then we went to... We made a Southern tour... We worked in Buffalo at the Vendome, and then we toured... We went all the way down to... How far did we go? We went to Georgia, Florida I think...
Did you have any bad experiences down there?

Oh, well...heh...it was... Not too many. The only thing is you couldn't get something to eat. I remember (who was in the band then?)...Cozy Cole or Bill Beeson couldn't get anything to eat, you know. And that was... You know, they described me as a very...as a madman! Called me The Mad Mexican, you know...

So said, "Look, I'm going to have something to eat." This was a place called Paintsville, Kentucky. I went out there when we got there, and I got something to eat. When I saw that, the whole bus was empty! I happened to be lucky to get two ladies that had a store, and I just got a bag of groceries, and when they saw me come out of the store with groceries, the bag in my hand...! [LAUGHS] I never saw a bus empty so fast.
